title: Open-Source Essential Mathematics for the Victorian Curriculum Year 9

chapters.title: Real Numbers, Surds, and Index Laws
chapters.description: Rational and irrational numbers on the real number line, simplifying surds, negative and zero integer exponents, and scientific notation.

sections.title: The Real Number System and Surds
sections.vcaa_description: Recognise that the real number system includes the rational numbers and the irrational numbers, and solve problems involving real numbers using digital tools.
sections.target_mastery: Classify real numbers, locate surds on the number line using geometric constructions, and simplify basic square-root surds.
prerequisites: Irrational numbers and square roots (Year 8 VC2M8N01)
sub_concepts: Real number hierarchy (N, Z, Q, R\Q, R)
Simplifying surds using square factors
Exact vs approximate decimal calculations

sections.title: Index Laws with Algebraic Bases and Negative Indices
sections.vcaa_description: Apply the exponent laws to numerical expressions with integer exponents and extend to variables.
sections.target_mastery: Simplify algebraic and numerical expressions using all index laws, including zero and negative integer indices a^(-n) = 1/a^n.
prerequisites: Index laws with positive integer exponents (Year 8 VC2M8N02)
sub_concepts: Index laws with pronumeral bases
Negative integer exponents and reciprocals
Products and quotients of algebraic powers

sections.title: Scientific Notation and Significant Figures
sections.vcaa_description: Solve problems involving very small and very large measurements, time scales and intervals expressed in scientific notation.
sections.target_mastery: Convert between standard decimal form and scientific notation a x 10^n, round to a given number of significant figures, and solve scientific measurement problems.
sub_concepts: Scientific notation for large and small numbers
Significant figures and metric prefixes (nano to tera)
Multiplying and dividing in scientific notation

chapters.title: Financial Mathematics and Direct Proportion
chapters.description: Wages, salaries, overtime, commission, Australian income tax tables, simple interest, and direct proportion modelling.

sections.title: Earning Income, Commission, and Australian Taxation
sections.vcaa_description: Use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving direct proportion, rates, ratios and percentages, including in financial contexts.
sections.target_mastery: Calculate gross pay including time-and-a-half/double-time overtime, tiered commission, leave loading (17.5%), and Australian PAYG progressive income tax.
sub_concepts: Wages, salaries, and overtime penalty rates
Retainers and tiered sales commission
Australian progressive income tax brackets and Medicare levy

sections.title: Simple Interest, Repayment Modelling, and Direct Proportion
sections.vcaa_description: Use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving direct proportion, rates, ratios and percentages, including in financial contexts.
sections.target_mastery: Transpose the simple interest formula I = Prt to find principal, rate, or time, and model direct variation y = kx.
sub_concepts: Rearranging I = Prt for P, r, and t
Hire-purchase and effective interest rates
Direct proportion y = kx and constant of proportionality

chapters.title: Algebraic Expansion and Factorisation
chapters.description: Expanding binomial products, perfect squares, difference of two squares, and factorising monic quadratic trinomials.

sections.title: Expanding Binomial Products and Special Identities
sections.vcaa_description: Simplify algebraic expressions, expand binomial products and factorise monic quadratic expressions.
sections.target_mastery: Expand binomial products (x + a)(x + b), perfect squares (a +/- b)^2, and difference of two squares (a - b)(a + b).
prerequisites: Distributive law and linear factorisation (Year 8 VC2M8A01)
sub_concepts: Expanding (ax + b)(cx + d) using the distributive law
Perfect square identities (a +/- b)^2 = a^2 +/- 2ab + b^2
Difference of two squares identity (a - b)(a + b) = a^2 - b^2

sections.title: Factorising Difference of Two Squares and Grouping
sections.vcaa_description: Simplify algebraic expressions, expand binomial products and factorise monic quadratic expressions.
sections.target_mastery: Factorise expressions by extracting common factors, grouping in pairs, and applying the difference of two squares identity.
sub_concepts: Common factor extraction before DOTS
Difference of two squares a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)
Factorising four-term expressions by grouping in pairs

sections.title: Factorising Monic Quadratic Trinomials
sections.vcaa_description: Simplify algebraic expressions, expand binomial products and factorise monic quadratic expressions.
sections.target_mastery: Factorise monic quadratic trinomials x^2 + bx + c by finding factor pairs of c that sum to b.
sub_concepts: Sum-and-product method for x^2 + bx + c
Handling negative constant terms and negative middle terms
Extracting a common numerical factor before trinomial factorisation

chapters.title: Linear Equations, Inequalities, and Coordinate Geometry
chapters.description: Linear equations with algebraic fractions, gradient, midpoint, distance between two points, parallel and perpendicular lines.

sections.title: Linear Equations with Fractions and Literal Equations
sections.vcaa_description: Use mathematical modelling to solve applied problems involving change, including linear relations.
sections.target_mastery: Solve multi-step linear equations involving algebraic fractions with binomial numerators and rearrange formulas.
sub_concepts: Clearing fractional denominators using the LCM
Cross-multiplication for rational equations
Transposing formulas for a specified variable

sections.title: Gradient, Midpoint, and Distance on the Cartesian Plane
sections.vcaa_description: Find the gradient of a line segment, the midpoint of a line segment and the distance between 2 points on the Cartesian plane, using a range of strategies, including digital tools.
sections.target_mastery: Calculate the gradient m, midpoint M, and exact length d of a line segment joining (x1, y1) and (x2, y2).
sub_concepts: Gradient formula m = (y2 - y1)/(x2 - x1)
Midpoint formula M = ((x1 + x2)/2, (y1 + y2)/2)
Distance formula d = sqrt((x2 - x1)^2 + (y2 - y1)^2)

sections.title: Equations of Straight Lines and Linear Modelling
sections.vcaa_description: Use mathematical modelling to solve applied problems involving change, including linear relations.
sections.target_mastery: Determine the equation of a straight line from two points or point and gradient, sketch using x- and y-intercepts, and model linear change.
sub_concepts: Gradient-intercept form y = mx + c and point-gradient form y - y1 = m(x - x1)
Sketching lines via dual intercepts
Horizontal (y = k) and vertical (x = h) lines

chapters.title: Quadratic Equations and Non-Linear Graphs
chapters.description: Null Factor Law, solving monic quadratic equations, graphing parabolas and circles, and algorithmic approximations.

sections.title: Solving Quadratic Equations via the Null Factor Law
sections.vcaa_description: Use the null factor law to solve monic quadratic equations with integer roots, and graph quadratic relations, identifying key features.
sections.target_mastery: Factorise monic quadratic equations and apply the Null Factor Law (ab = 0 => a = 0 or b = 0) to find roots.
sub_concepts: The Null Factor Law
Rearranging quadratics into standard form x^2 + bx + c = 0
Modelling area and projectile problems with quadratic equations

sections.title: Graphing Quadratic Relations and Key Features of Parabolas
sections.vcaa_description: Use the null factor law to solve monic quadratic equations with integer roots, and graph quadratic relations, identifying key features.
sections.target_mastery: Sketch parabolas y = a(x - h)^2 + k and y = (x - p)(x - q), identifying the turning point, axis of symmetry, y-intercept, and x-intercepts.
sub_concepts: Dilation, reflection, and translation of y = x^2
Turning point form y = a(x - h)^2 + k
Intercept form and axis of symmetry x = (p + q)/2

sections.title: Non-Linear Relations and Algorithmic Root Approximation
sections.vcaa_description: Experiment with the effects of the parameters on the graphs of non-linear relations, and use algorithms and digital tools to approximate solutions.
sections.target_mastery: Explore graphs of simple exponential and reciprocal relations and apply the bisection/systematic trial algorithm to approximate non-integer roots.
sub_concepts: Comparing linear, quadratic, and exponential growth
Bisection algorithm for approximating irrational roots
Parameter exploration with digital graphing tools

chapters.title: Surface Area and Volume of Cylinders, Prisms, and Composite Solids
chapters.description: Total surface area and volume of right prisms and cylinders, composite solids, and absolute/percentage measurement error.

sections.title: Surface Area of Right Prisms and Cylinders
sections.vcaa_description: Solve problems involving the volume and surface area of right prisms and cylinders using appropriate units.
sections.target_mastery: Calculate the total and curved surface area of right prisms, cylinders (TSA = 2*pi*r^2 + 2*pi*r*h), and composite solids.
prerequisites: Area of circles and composite shapes (Year 8 VC2M8M01, VC2M8M03)
sub_concepts: Nets of right prisms and cylinders
Curved vs total surface area of open and closed cylinders
Surface area of composite 3D solids

sections.title: Volume of Cylinders, Composite Solids, and Error in Measurement
sections.vcaa_description: Solve problems involving the volume and surface area of right prisms and cylinders using appropriate units; calculate absolute, relative and percentage errors in measurements (VC2M9M05).
sections.target_mastery: Calculate the volume of cylinders (V = pi*r^2*h) and composite solids, and determine limits of accuracy, absolute error, and percentage error.
sub_concepts: Volume of cylinders and hollow pipes (annular prisms)
Limits of accuracy (+/- 0.5 of smallest unit)
Absolute, relative, and percentage error (VC2M9M05)

chapters.title: Similarity, Scale Factors, and Geometric Reasoning
chapters.description: Similarity tests for triangles, area and volume scale factors (k, k^2, k^3), Euler's formula for polyhedra, and geometric algorithms.

sections.title: Similar Triangles and Geometric Proofs
sections.vcaa_description: Establish the conditions for similarity of triangles and use them to solve problems and prove geometric properties (including VC2M9SP01 angle properties).
sections.target_mastery: Prove triangles are similar using AAA, SAS, SSS, and RHS similarity tests and calculate unknown side lengths in overlapping triangles.
sub_concepts: Four similarity tests for triangles (AAA, SAS, SSS, RHS)
Finding unknown lengths using equal ratios of corresponding sides
Deductive angle and similarity proofs (VC2M9SP01)

sections.title: Scale Factors for Length, Area, and Volume, and Polyhedra
sections.vcaa_description: Solve problems involving the ratio of corresponding sides of similar figures, and the relationships between length, area and volume of similar figures and solids.
sections.target_mastery: Apply the area scale factor k^2 and volume scale factor k^3 to similar 2D figures and 3D solids, and verify Euler's formula V - E + F = 2 (VC2M9SP03).
sub_concepts: Linear scale factor k, area ratio k^2, and volume ratio k^3
Enlargements and reductions on the Cartesian plane
Polyhedra nets and Euler's formula V - E + F = 2 (VC2M9SP03)

chapters.title: Pythagoras' Theorem and Right-Angled Trigonometry
chapters.description: 3D applications of Pythagoras' theorem, trigonometric ratios (sine, cosine, tangent), finding unknown sides and angles, and angles of elevation and depression.

sections.title: Trigonometric Ratios (SOHCAHTOA) and Finding Side Lengths
sections.vcaa_description: Use similarity to investigate the constancy of the sine, cosine and tangent ratios for a given angle in right-angled triangles, and use trigonometric ratios and Pythagoras' theorem to solve right-angled triangle problems.
sections.target_mastery: Define sin, cos, and tan in right-angled triangles and use them to calculate unknown side lengths when the unknown is in the numerator or denominator.
sub_concepts: Labelling Hypotenuse, Opposite, and Adjacent sides
Sine, cosine, and tangent ratios (SOHCAHTOA)
Calculating unknown sides (unknown in numerator vs denominator)

sections.title: Inverse Trigonometry, Elevation, Depression, and Bearings
sections.vcaa_description: Use trigonometric ratios and Pythagoras' theorem to solve right-angled triangle problems.
sections.target_mastery: Use inverse trigonometric functions (sin^-1, cos^-1, tan^-1) to find acute angles and solve applied problems involving angles of elevation, depression, and compass bearings.
sub_concepts: Inverse trigonometric functions for finding angles
Angles of elevation and depression (alternate angles on horizontal lines)
Navigation and true bearings in right-angled triangles

chapters.title: Multi-Stage Probability and Relative Frequency
chapters.description: Two- and three-step chance experiments with and without replacement, tree diagrams, arrays, conditional language ('given that'), and simulations.

sections.title: Two-Step Experiments With and Without Replacement
sections.vcaa_description: List all outcomes for compound events both with and without replacement, using lists, tree diagrams, tables or arrays; assign probabilities to outcomes.
sections.target_mastery: Construct lattice arrays and probability tree diagrams for two-step experiments with and without replacement and calculate compound probabilities.
prerequisites: Venn diagrams and two-way tables (Year 8 VC2M8P02)
sub_concepts: Sample space arrays for independent events
Tree diagrams with replacement vs without replacement
Multiplying along branches and adding mutually exclusive paths

sections.title: Relative Frequency, 'And/Or' Compound Events, and Simulations
sections.vcaa_description: Calculate relative frequencies from given or collected data to estimate probabilities of events involving 'and', inclusive 'or' and exclusive 'or' (and design simulations VC2M9P03).
sections.target_mastery: Estimate compound probabilities from survey and experimental data using the Addition Rule Pr(A union B) = Pr(A) + Pr(B) - Pr(A intersect B) and multi-trial simulations.
sub_concepts: Inclusive 'or' vs exclusive 'or'
The Addition Rule for probability
Designing multi-step chance simulations (VC2M9P03)

chapters.title: Statistics, Back-to-Back Displays, and Bivariate Data
chapters.description: Sampling critiques in media reports, grouped frequency histograms, back-to-back stem-and-leaf plots, quartiles and IQR, and bivariate scatterplots.

sections.title: Grouped Histograms, Back-to-Back Stem Plots, and Quartiles
sections.vcaa_description: Represent the distribution of multiple data sets for numerical variables using comparative representations; compare data distributions with consideration of centre, spread and shape (including VC2M9ST01, VC2M9ST04).
sections.target_mastery: Construct and compare back-to-back stem-and-leaf plots and grouped histograms, and calculate the five-number summary and Interquartile Range (IQR = Q3 - Q1).
prerequisites: Summary statistics and distribution shape (Year 8 VC2M8ST01-03)
sub_concepts: Five-number summary (Min, Q1, Median, Q3, Max) and IQR
Back-to-back stem-and-leaf plots and parallel dot plots
Critiquing statistical claims and sampling bias in media reports (VC2M9ST01, VC2M9ST04)

sections.title: Bivariate Data, Two-Way Associations, and Scatterplots
sections.vcaa_description: Analyse how different sampling methods can affect the results of a statistical investigation; plan and conduct statistical investigations involving bivariate data (VC2M9ST05).
sections.target_mastery: Plot bivariate numerical data on a scatterplot and describe the direction (positive/negative), form (linear/non-linear), and strength (strong/moderate/weak) of association.
sub_concepts: Explanatory (independent) and response (dependent) variables
Constructing and interpreting scatterplots
Correlation vs causation in statistical investigations (VC2M9ST05)
